County Code § 82-5B
Prohibits parking watercraft, motor homes,
campers, trailers, vehicles ≥ 3 axles, vehicles
≥ 12,000 lbs., and vehicles transporting ≥ 16
passengers (except school buses).
QUALIFICATIONS:
 Residential public road
AND
 2000 linear feet or 5 block face minimum for
petition, whichever is less (New Districts only)
OR
Supervisor requested large area application

County Code § 82-5A
Prohibits parking along designated streets within a
District without a District Permit.
QUALIFICATIONS:
1) Distance:
Residential public road within 2,000 ft. walking distance
from pedestrian entrance or 1,000 ft. from the property
boundary of a High School, existing or proposed Rail
Station, or existing Virginia College or University
OR
2) Parking Demand Study:
* Minimum of 100 contiguous parking spaces required
(New District only)
 > 75% of spaces occupied
AND
 > 50% of those vehicles are non-residents

County Code § 82-5-7
Parking the following vehicles in residential districts is prohibited:
• Vehicles that exceed size and weight limits of:
More than 21 feet long, more than 8 feet high, including
appurtenances, width of 102 in. or more, or gross
vehicle weight of 12,000 or more pounds.
Examples of vehicles exempt from these height and weight limits are
commercial vehicles used by public service company, watercraft or
motor home (unless in a CPD), school buses, personal vehicles
used for transporting persons with disabilities and contracted moving
vehicles for 48 hours. (Link to additional exceptions below)
• Any vehicle licensed as a common or contract carrier or limousine
One resident of each single family dwelling unit may park one
vehicle licensed and registered in the Commonwealth of Virginia
as a taxicab or limousine (see additional information below)
• Vehicles carrying commercial freight in plain view,
• Trailer or semitrailer except camper, boat or *single axle utility
• Any Vehicle with 3 or more axles
* "Utility trailer" means: A small non-motorized trailer which is generally
pulled by a motorized vehicle and features an open-top cargo area.

By petition:
1. HOA submits request to District Supervisor*
2. District Supervisor forwards request to FCDOT
3. FCDOT issues petition and area map, if eligible
4. Signatures gathered verifying ≥60% support from
entire area and >50% on each block
5. Completed petition returned to Supervisor with
fee of $10 per petitioning address signature
6. Supervisor forwards petition and fees to FCDOT
for review
7. Board of Supervisors conduct public hearing on
proposed parking district
8.If approved, FCDOT installs signs delineating
prohibitions, as required
By Large Area application:
Contact District Supervisor
* If no HOA, signed by 10 residences or 60% of
affected residences, whichever is less

1. HOA submits request to District Supervisor*
2. District Supervisor forwards request to FCDOT
3. FCDOT reviews road(s), documenting eligibility for
restriction and parking demand study, if required
4. FCDOT issues petition and area map, if eligible
5. Signatures gathered verifying ≥60% support from
entire area and >50% for each block face
6. Completed petition returned to Supervisor with fee of
$10 per petitioning address signature
7. Supervisor forwards petition and fees to FCDOT for
review
8. Board of Supervisors conduct public hearing on
proposed parking district
9. If approved, FCDOT installs “No Parking Except by
Permit” signs
10.Eligible residents apply for permits
* If no HOA, signed by 10 residences or 60% of affected
residences, whichever is less
